scores.evidence: Title asks one question (what happens when the owner clicks Send). The subtitle names the audience (new engineers) and scope (sendMessage only).
Boxes are mostly runtime units with a type tag. 'Owner' is a person, not a unit, and Postgres is filed under 'Third parties' with the vendor APIs, which is a little odd.

Scope is tight, and the out-of-scope items (Exa/Apollo/LLM, X DMs) are listed at the bottom. There is no visible order of steps (claim, then gates, then send), even though order is the whole question. The worker's own DB or status reporting path is not shown.

Edges have labels and use solid for sync and dashed for async. But start/poll is shown only as a footnote marker, 'F1'. The claim/mark and check+send lines run horizontally through the Fly.io worker frame, so they look like they come from the worker. The 'invite / DM' label sits far from its line. Nothing is numbered, so the order is lost.
Four labelled frames: local device, Vercel host, Fly container, external. The managed vs self-run distinction is in text. Edges cutting through the Fly frame blur that boundary.

Reads left to right, but the diagram fills only about 60% of the canvas. Body text is roughly 8–9px at 1194x834 and hard to read. Orthogonal lines overlap and cross the worker frame, and the large empty frame space wastes room.

The key explains frames, boxes, solid/dashed/dotted and caller→recipient. But everything is the same red, so nothing but text separates managed from external. The 'All generated ink is AI red; user additions are blue' line is tool chrome, not something a reader of the system needs. Dotted is in the key but never used.

Notes cover fail-open reply check vs fail-closed in-touch check, the daily limit, the one-time claim, the serial lock, the 75s wait then polling, the exit-node wait with a 24h timeout, and no retry after restarts. None of this is attached to the components it describes, and Gmail-down behavior isn't covered.

Dated, with revision f467a33 + local edits, and it says outright that the live system was not checked and the owner is 'Unassigned', so nobody is accountable. The claims I spot-checked match lib/engine.ts (status 'sending', daily limit, checkReplies .catch(()=>0), resolveLinkedinSend 75_000).

A newcomer gets the gist from the notes. But without a walkthrough, the routing makes it easy to think the Fly worker calls Postgres and Gmail, the order of the gates isn't visible, and the small text slows reading.

coldRead: The owner clicks Send in their browser, which calls sendMessage in the Next.js app on Vercel. sendMessage claims the draft in Postgres by setting it to 'sending' so it is claimed only once, then checks the daily limit. It checks Gmail for replies; if that check errors, it counts as no reply and the send goes ahead (fails open). It then checks whether the owner is already in touch with the person; if that check errors, the send is blocked (fails closed). For email, the app sends through the Gmail API and marks the row sent. For LinkedIn, it starts a run on a single serial Python/browser-use worker on Fly. The worker drives Chromium through the owner's home Tailscale exit node, waiting up to 24h for that route, and sends the invite or DM. The app waits 75s for the result, after which later polls resolve rows still marked 'sending'. Runs cut off by a restart are marked failed, not retried. Prospecting and X DMs are out of scope.
inaccuracies: The claim/mark (web→Postgres) and check+send (web→Gmail) lines run horizontally through the Fly.io worker frame, which suggests the worker talks to Postgres and Gmail. sendMessage in lib/engine.ts makes those calls from the web app.
Postgres is grouped under 'Third parties / vendor services'. The map gives no hosting evidence for that, and it misleads about who owns the data.
start/poll is shown only as 'F1'. Polling also happens later from refresh (lib/engine.ts:1758–1764, resolveLinkedinSend with 0 wait), which is a separately started event and is not drawn.
Order matters in lib/engine.ts (~1323–1393: claim, daily limit, reply check, in-touch check, then send), but the edges show no order.
The key defines a dotted style that is never used and includes a line about the authoring tool's colors that says nothing about the system.
improvements: Number the steps on the edges (1 claim, 2 limit, 3 reply check, 4 in-touch check, 5a Gmail send / 5b start worker, 6 poll/mark) and draw the later refresh poll as its own dashed edge.

Re-route the web→Postgres and web→Gmail lines around the Fly frame, or move Fly below Third parties. Put start/poll back as an inline label instead of the F1 footnote, and keep 'invite / DM' next to its line.

Fill the canvas and raise the body text to at least 11px. Use a non-color signal for external vs self-run (shape or fill), drop the tool-chrome key text, and attach each note to the component it describes. Name an owner.
